entries.text: I’ll check the recent work and open changes for a useful next step.

My vote: **make a one-minute Note(s)pat(ial) rehearsal we love.** The six-seat score and section renderer already exist. Pick one passage, listen and watch, then tune its movement, timing, and screen response until it feels right.

Two other good options:

- **Small, useful win:** drop a painting onto the desktop app and open it in `nopaint`.
- **Reliability:** measure spatial playback drift—the rehearsal docs still list output latency and drift as uncalibrated.

I’d start with the music. A finished minute gives us something concrete to judge.

The opening, waltz, lullaby, and ending have long stretches without percussion. I’ll give each a pattern that follows its meter and tempo, and keep a light pulse under the pauses so the rhythm carries through.

Percussion now runs through all eleven chapters, including the opening and the pauses. The melodies and cue times are preserved, and all 11,100 events pass the playback check. I’m rendering the full version to audition in QuickTime.

The added percussion follows the opening’s acceleration, the waltz’s three beats, and the lullaby’s six eighths. The full render is still encoding; I also caught a tempo label that needs rounding to stay readable.

/bin/zsh -lc "python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
p = Path('grants/culturehub-la-2026/NOTESPATIAL-ARRANGEMENT.md')
s = p.read_text()
changes = {
'A tune in the hands, twice. Then the ring hops': 'Taps mark all three beats. A tune in the hands, twice. Then the ring hops',
'a cluster, a crash. Silence. The hands': 'a cluster, a crash. Percussion holds the gap. The hands',
'Two beats of nothing.': 'Two beats of percussion alone.',
'The cradle thins to nothing.': 'The cradle thins over soft thumps and brushed eighths.',
'into a beat and a half of silence.': 'into a beat and a half of percussion alone.',
'Two directions, then nothing': 'Two directions, then percussion alone',
'General pause.': 'Percussion bridges the melodic pause.',
'A stinger. Silence.': 'A stinger; taps carry into the Return.',
'bass, pads, taps, the walk narrows': 'bass, pads, the larger taps; the walk narrows',
'**9:12** — the tutti D chord from all six, then the pause.': '**9:12** — the tutti D chord from all six, then percussion alone.',
}
for old,new in changes.items():
    assert old in s, old
    s=s.replace(old,new)
p.write_text(s)
PY" · done
The revised score stays within the playback limit at 20 simultaneous voices. I’m finishing the render with the corrected tempo label, then opening it for you to hear.

Added percussion throughout—all eleven chapters, from the first bell through the final knock. Patterns follow each section’s meter and tempo.

Rebuilt and checked the score, then opened the revised full arrangement in QuickTime.

I’ll trace the newer instruments and speaker setup, then make sure the next render includes them alongside the continuous percussion. I’ll also check how the subwoofer and kick should fit the score and playback model.

- Mallet ensemble: vibraphone, marimba, kalimba, xylophone, gamelan
- Native ensemble: flute, harp, piano, synth bass and brass

For the kick, do you mean a synthesized kick in the score, or a physical kick drum in the room model?
- Synthesized kick, feeding the subwoofer too
- Physical kick drum shown in the room

I found why the last video missed them: the working composer and renderer no longer include the recently committed instrument support. I’m bringing that support back while keeping the percussion changes. The subwoofer receiver already has a bass-and-kick feed, so I can use its behavior as the render’s reference.

I’ll use the mallet ensemble for this pass and treat the kick as synthesized. I also found a subwoofer bug: the newer bass harmonics and kick click could make its score loader reject the arrangement. I’ve adjusted it to select the low-frequency content, and I’m adding that filtered feed and a visible SUB cabinet to the video.

/bin/zsh -lc "python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
p=Path('fedac/native/tools/notespatial-native-render.mjs')
s=p.read_text()
a=s.index('  const inputs = [], graph = [];')
b=s.index(\"if (flag('audio-only'))\",a)
s=s[:a]+s[a:b].replace('SEATS','OUTPUTS')+s[b:]
p.write_text(s)
PY" · done

/bin/zsh -lc "python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
p=Path('grants/culturehub-la-2026/NOTESPATIAL-ARRANGEMENT.md')
current=p.read_text()
s=subprocess.check_output(['git','show','HEAD:'+str(p)],text=True)
s=s.replace('cartoon score is, with stingers and silences. What ties them: the theme','cartoon score is, with stingers and melodic rests. Percussion carries the\\nbeat through every chapter and transition. What ties them: the theme')
for key in ['I','III','IV','V','VI','VII','IX','X','XI']:
    prefix='| '+key+' |'
    new=next(l for l in current.splitlines() if l.startswith(prefix))
    old=next(l for l in s.splitlines() if l.startswith(prefix))
    s=s.replace(old,new)
s=s.replace('General pause.','Percussion bridges the melodic pause.')
a=s.index('Measured on the binaural render')
b=s.index('## Instruments',a)
s=s[:a]+'''Percussion follows each chapter's tempo: three beats in the Waltz, two
thumps with six brushed eighths in the Lullaby, a quarter-note pulse
elsewhere. Existing kit attacks take precedence. The melodic pauses
retain the pulse; the Return sheds its larger tap pattern but keeps quiet
time through the Vanish's final knock. "'`--kick` adds a restrained kick on
the main steps throughout; the Lift keeps its written kit.

The mallets-and-kick score has 17,018 events and peaks at 28 simultaneous
voices against the runtime'"'s 32-voice limit.

'''+s[b:]
s=s.replace('the first bell from the held laptop alone.','the held voice over percussion from the first beat.')
s=s.replace('the first tap lands on the downbeat the scale lap set up.','the Walk\\'s fuller taps land on the downbeat the scale lap set up.')
s=s.replace('the tutti D chord from all six, then the pause.','the tutti D chord from all six, then percussion alone.')
pos=s.index('## Listen for, at the tech')
s=s[:pos]+'''## Mallets, kick and SUB preview

"'```sh
node fedac/native/tools/compose-notespatial-native.mjs --voicing mallets --kick
node fedac/native/tools/notespatial-native-check.mjs fedac/native/scores/notespatial-native-mallets-kick.nsscore
node fedac/native/tools/notespatial-native-render.mjs fedac/native/scores/notespatial-native-mallets-kick.nsscore --sub --out grants/culturehub-la-2026/notespatial-native-mallets-kick-sub.mp4
```

The video shows the instrument families, a kick hit indicator, and a SUB
cabinet whose cone follows its filtered signal. SUB uses the receiver'"'s
bass/kick selection one octave down, 25 Hz high-pass, two 80 Hz low-pass
sections, and 25% level. Its compressor is approximated. "'`--sub-level`,
`--sub-cutoff` and `--sub-az` adjust the model; the assumed position is at
the front, outside the laptop ring. It stays fixed when the field turns.
Room acoustics, device response and receiver latency are not simulated.
`--solo sub --audio-only` exports the SUB alone for inspection.

For live rehearsal, start the receiver with
`SUB_SCORE=fedac/native/scores/notespatial-native-mallets-kick.nsscore node fedac/native/tools/sub-receiver/server.mjs`
and deploy that same score to the six laptops. This render does not deploy
to the room or publish an OS update.

'"'''+s[pos:]
p.write_text(s)
PY" · done

The preview now includes the mallet instruments, a kick indicator, and a SUB cabinet driven by the filtered bass signal. All 17,018 score events pass playback checks, and polyphony stays at 28 of 32 voices. I’m encoding the full version and preparing the code and scores to commit and push.
